existing_tips: Inseparable prefix 'be-': no 'ge-' in past participle – bestehen → bestanden.
Two traps: weil (because) and dass (that). Both push the verb to the back. Weil er müde ist – not we
'eines Geschenks' – genitive case showing possession. Masculine/neuter nouns add -s or -es.
Perfekt with 'sein': verbs of movement/change use 'sein' – 'ist geflogen'.
Use `möchte` whenever you'd say 'I'd like' in English. The verb form is technically subjunctive of `
'Der' before a feminine noun in dative – 'die' becomes 'der' in dative case: 'mit der Frau', 'in der
'Zwischen' + dative: location – 'zwischen der Post und dem Rathaus'.
'Nicht' vs 'kein': use 'keinen Kaffee' (negating noun) but 'nicht einschlafen' (negating verb).
Separable: auf·geben → auf·ge·geben – 'ge-' between prefix and stem.
Dative: 'gefallen' takes dative – 'dem Kind'. German says 'the gift pleases to the child'.
Inseparable prefix verbs (be-, er-, ver-, ent-) form their participle without 'ge-': besucht, erzähl
'Mir geht es gut' uses dative 'mir' – literally 'to me it goes well'.
The dative case marks indirect objects and follows certain prepositions (mit, von, zu, bei, nach, au
